definitions.explanation: A condition or factor that limits freedom of action. Used for rules, conditions, budgets, time limits, and other factors that restrict what can be done.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}の{制約|せいやく}がある。
{予算|よさん}の{制約|せいやく}の{中|なか}で{工夫|くふう}する。
examples.english: To work creatively within budget constraints.

examples.japanese: {法律|ほうりつ}による{制約|せいやく}があるため、この{土地|とち}には{高|たか}い{建物|たてもの}を{建|た}てることができない。
examples.english: Due to legal restrictions, tall buildings cannot be built on this land.

notes:
A formal word commonly used in business, technical, and academic contexts. Often used in the pattern {制約|せいやく}の{中|なか}で (within constraints) or {制約|せいやく}を{受|う}ける (to be subject to restrictions).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{時間|じかん}の{制約|せいやく}: time constraint
・{予算|よさん}の{制約|せいやく}: budget constraint
・{制約|せいやく}を{受|う}ける: to be subject to restrictions
・{制約|せいやく}{条件|じょうけん}: limiting conditions
